newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs end nearly flat after range-bound trade.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs end nearly flat after range-bound trade.

text.p: The composite stock index ended Thursday's trading nearly flat after a dull session brightened only by foreign interest in KEPCO shares, brokers said.
The index rose 0.77 of a point to a provisional close of 744.91. Despite the rise, declining shares beat advancers 492 to 347, while 23.89 million shares changed hands.
"The market is still very weak and fragile," said a Dongsuh Securities broker. "We'll see some more decline, but I think we're very close to the bottom."
Many brokers have forecast that the market would find its feet at around the 720 mark.
Interest in Korea Electric Power (KEPCO) dragged the index to its positive close. The shares gained 1,000 won to 27,900.

"The market is up because of KEPCO," said Choi Tae-hwan, head of sales at KLB Securities. "Foreigners are really getting fed up with the market, and are shifting out of banks and securities and into KEPCO, which is seen as a safe stock."
Banks and securities shares were hard hit by selling. Korea Exchange Bank fell 130 won to 7,820, Hanil Bank lost 170 won to 6,200, and Daewoo Securities shed 200 won to 14,000.
Rumours that the Sammi Group was in financial difficulties hit Sammi Steel shares. The stock fell 270 won to a low of 4,320. Company officials could not immediately be reached.
The government's plan to hold an auction this year to sell Korea Telecom shares and to publicly list the shares next year did not excite investors, brokers said.
"There's not much reaction. The market is so bearish that investors expect the government to push the listing off again anyways," said Choi. Two previous auctions on the company were undersubscribed.
